paragraphs: Rabbah bar Hanan bar Abba, Rav's grandson and Rav Hisda's brother-in-law. He follows his own approach (see Rav Hanan bar Abba), but I showed there that he erred: this Rabbah was bar Rav Hanan bar Rava, for Rav Hanan bar Rava was Rav's son-in-law and Rav Hisda's father-in-law. This Rava, Rav Hanan's father, was an earlier figure. (He came to R' Abbahu the Second—see there—Yuhasin under aleph; I have not found it.) Abaye asked Rabbah, ‘Someone like the master, whom all Pumbedita hates’—because he rebuked them in heavenly matters, since they were deceitful, as found in Hullin—‘who will warm his eulogy?’ He answered, ‘You and Rabbah bar Rav Hanan suffice me’: Mo'ed Katan; Shabbat 153a. He spoke to Abaye: Eruvin 14, end of b, 68a, 75b; Shabbat 148; Beitzah 30a; Bekhorot 54a; Menahot 14b; Keritot 18b. He called Abaye ‘tarda’—fool; another explanation: lazy. Tosafot write that Abaye was his colleague, as found in Keitzad Mevarkhin 46. He asked Abaye, “Has the master heard?” (Eruvin 38b reads Rabbah bar Rav Hanin). He asked Abaye, “Does the master object from Rabbi Eliezer?” (Eruvin 45a names the questioner as Rabbah bar bar Hana). He spoke to Abaye; some say to Rav Yosef and R' Avya the Elder: Sanhedrin 34b. He regularly came from Artivna to Pumbedita every Shabbat. Abaye asked him, ‘What is your reasoning?’ Eruvin 51, end of b. Rava, R' Zeira, and Abaye were sitting there, 92a. He had a palm on the boundary of Rav Yosef's orchard, and Rav Yosef told him, ‘Go cut it down’: Bava Batra 26a. He taught before Rava: Zevahim 55, beginning of a. He spoke to Rava: Menahot 40a. His host asked him a question. He did not know the answer and consulted Rava (Beitzah 12b). Several of these places have Rava bar Hanan. It would appear he was named for his paternal grandfather; but most places have Rabbah bar Hanan.
